beats.title: One missing reconciliation — the office task
beats.purpose: Start immediately where Episode02 ended, no morning recap or Soniya cutaways.
beats.action: A client asks for a corrected December management-report pack before its next-day board presentation. Two vendor payments look duplicated in the import; this is a reconciliation question, not asserted fraud or a legal filing deadline. Taniya assigns a clean evidence trail. Neha delivers source exports. New Year's office staffing is already part of the working plan.
beats.visual: Taniya is in the same CA-office clothes she changed into during TS07; proposed visual only: muted blouse, tailored dark trousers, neatly managed hair, work tote and an ID lanyard. Exact color stays unlocked.

beats.turn: Her competence, not a random personal event, drives the afternoon.

beats.title: Raghav vs Chirag — same file, different instincts
beats.purpose: Establish the 'office twins' narrative pairing without lying about kinship.
beats.action: Raghav wants to close the duplicate as an import error quickly; Chirag quietly spots that the payment reference format differs. Taniya makes them compare the source bank extract, invoice and journal. They are a familiar working duo, NOT actual brothers or twins. She has previously exchanged playful work banter with both, so introductions are skipped. The three lean over a shared screen to review but there is no staged clothing accident or forced touch.

beats.title: Punit — the office Chotu-type gets his own competence
beats.location: CA office · archive cabinet and scan desk
beats.purpose: Give the younger office helper a meaningful role, not another gaze-only scene.
beats.action: Punit retrieves the earlier original export and its update timestamp. He does not read private files outside permission. His method establishes that one duplicate-looking row is an imported reversal, and the correct reconciliation needs a verified journal note. Taniya thanks him; his admiration remains mostly quiet and unacted. This is not a new staffer called Chotu.
beats.visual: Punit lays out two labeled printouts without touching Taniya's personal belongings. The office hum, stapler and ledger provide concrete texture.

beats.title: Pradeep Khanna — the older mentor's challenge
beats.purpose: One old-man office figure with credible authority and a nonsexual story consequence.
beats.action: Pradeep asks why Taniya did not simply delete the extra line. She shows the original export and journal evidence and recommends retaining audit traceability. He initially questions whether she is overcomplicating a routine error but accepts the proof. Raghav sees her defend her conclusion without needing him to answer for her. Attraction or inappropriate touch from the senior is NOT asserted.
beats.visual: Taniya stays standing beside the open case file until invited to sit; Pradeep marks the supporting entry and signs off the next review step.

beats.turn: Professional reversal is the surprise; it avoids a manufactured sexual accident or abuse of authority.

cast: Mr. Mehra (60, client advisor, remote voice)
beats.purpose: Differentiate firm partner from senior client advisor; do not copy Pradeep's mentor beat.
beats.action: Client advisor Mehra wants the revised numbers sent before the next meeting; firm partner Vivek Suri asks Taniya to distinguish an unresolved anomaly from an actual double payment. She explains the bank source and asks for the required written confirmation. Partner approves a conditional note, rather than pressuring the team to hide a finding. Both older men remain professionally grounded; no new concealed romance is claimed as canon.

During a natural side-by-side screen handover Raghav is closer than usual; Taniya notices and repositions her chair comfortably. No accidental physical touch, no attraction asserted as established. Other office colleagues continue their actual roles rather than having a multi-hour flirting scene.
